title: POP3 uses transient message numbers as stable UIDs
reasoning: Search results expose uid as the POP3 message index, and later fetches convert that uid back to an index for RETR. POP3 message numbers are session-order positions and can change when mailbox contents change, so a search result link can fetch a different message or fail after another client deletes mail. POP3 provides UIDL for stable IDs, but this connector does not use it.
recommendation: Use POP3 UIDL values as exposed message UIDs, maintain a UIDL-to-index lookup per operation when fetching, and keep the current numeric index only as an internal retrieval detail.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked POP3 tests are included, and the issue requires simulating mailbox renumbering between search and fetch.
suggestedRegressionTest: Fake a POP3 server where UIDL values remain stable while message numbers shift between search and fetch, and assert fetch_message retrieves by UIDL rather than by stale index.
minimumFixScope: Change POP3 summary UID generation and fetch/raw/attachment lookup to resolve UIDL to the current message number.
